question: Can a language model pretrained only on equation structures from a mathematical handbook provide a useful prior over free-form partial differential equations, then be steered by observations to recover compact governing laws more broadly and efficiently than fixed-library or tree-search methods?

key_findings.claim: EqGPT turns handbook equations into a reusable structural prior, but its validity constraints are mainly grammatical rather than physical.
key_findings.evidence: The authors manually reduce 221 handbook PDE structures to 56 operator and term tokens, augment each structure to 32 order permutations for 7,072 sequences, and train a GPT-2-like next-token model. Generation alternates term and operator positions, masks variables absent from the target dimension, injects 20% uniform valid-token exploration, and stops at an end token or length 50; these rules do not themselves enforce dimensional consistency, conservation laws, boundary conditions, or well-posedness.

anchors.section: Materials and Methods / EqGPT and SAT
Materials and Methods / SAT generation constraints

key_findings.claim: The data-conditioned search is an elite-sampling loop over surrogate-derived derivatives, not direct conditional equation generation.
key_findings.evidence: A neural surrogate first interpolates observations and supplies automatic-differentiation features. Each cycle samples 400 structures, obtains coefficients by least squares, scores sparsity-weighted R-squared, fine-tunes for five epochs on the best ten structures at learning rate 1e-5, and retains the best ten from the old and new pools; five cycles are used. Optional PINN refinement then changes coefficients but not the selected structure.

key_findings.claim: On the paper's eight canonical examples, EqGPT covers every displayed structure in tens of seconds, whereas the selected baselines are faster when applicable but leave several nonstandard forms unsupported or incorrect.
key_findings.evidence: Figure 3 reports EqGPT times of 11.47-37.83 seconds and correct recovery in all eight displayed cases. Sparse methods take 0.168-3.069 seconds on applicable equations but are marked unavailable or incorrect on most mixed-derivative, fractional, and compound forms; DISCOVER takes 13.31-1,359 seconds on its applicable cases and LLM4ED takes 128.2-1,654 seconds. All methods receive metadata from the same trained surrogate, so this comparison isolates structure search rather than end-to-end handling of raw noise.

anchors.section: Comparison against existing PDE discovery algorithms

key_findings.claim: The handbook prior helps on held-out target structures, but the ablations are small and show dependence on the breadth of the handbook corpus.
key_findings.evidence: Across ten seeds per equation, deleting the target equation still gives at least 0.7 success in the eight canonical cases, while including it is usually slightly better and Chaffee-Infante is the most affected. With zero handbook equations, the three-structure ablation never succeeds; success generally rises with 5, 10, 25, 50, 100, 150, 200, and 220 training equations and reaches 0.8-1.0 at the largest settings.

key_findings.claim: The irregular-domain and higher-dimensional demonstrations establish broad representational reach, but mostly as one-off reconstruction examples rather than statistically replicated benchmarks.
key_findings.evidence: The method recovers Poisson equations on a disk, a punctured smiley-face region, discontinuous EITech glyphs, and a 3D shuttle, with 0.63% reported coefficient error on the shuttle. It also returns near-ground-truth structures for 2D Burgers, an H-shaped membrane, and coupled 3D oil-water flow, including expanded interaction terms for nested divergence operators. The figures show one optimization trajectory per setting and report no seed distribution or uncertainty interval for these cases.

key_findings.claim: Two displayed simulation specifications contain source errors that must be repaired before independent reuse.
key_findings.evidence: Equation 7 prints the H-membrane initial field as 2 exp[-125(x-0.25)^2 + (y-0.5)^2], whose positive y-square term is inconsistent with the localized two-dimensional peak in Figure 5b; the likely intended exponent is -125[(x-0.25)^2+(y-0.5)^2]. The shuttle supplement gives x in [7.65,7.04], an impossible reversed interval, while the public preprocessing code uses [-7.65,7.04]. The later version-of-record supplement repeats both defects rather than resolving them.

key_findings.claim: The compact oil-water equations are not mathematically well typed as printed, although their expanded forms expose a plausible intended Darcy operator.
key_findings.evidence: Equations 8-9 write an outer gradient rather than divergence, join scalar permeability K to the inner gradient with a dot, and subtract acceleration vector g directly from scalar pressure P. Equations 10-11 and Figure 5 retain related notation, while expanded Equations 12-13 align with the intended product rule for divergence of K times a pressure-gradient-minus-gravity term. The recovery therefore supports an expanded term pattern, not the literal validity of every compact displayed equation.

key_findings.claim: Noise robustness depends strongly on the equation and surrogate regime rather than supporting a universal high-noise guarantee.
key_findings.evidence: Figure 2 reports correct canonical structures at 50% or more noise in most one-dimensional cases, but Supplementary Table S2 shows the 2D Burgers coefficients changing from about 1.01/1.01 at zero noise to 1.87/2.07 at 15% noise and adding a large spurious term at 20%. The Allen-Cahn grid succeeds at 50% noise only for at least 1,000 samples, and fails at 75% noise for every displayed sample count.

key_findings.claim: The wave-tank case yields a compact empirical evolution law across twelve experiments, but it is not an independent discovery-and-validation split and its coefficient-sign convention is unresolved.
key_findings.evidence: The selected law combines first-order propagation, a linear third derivative, and a third derivative of squared elevation. Each candidate's reward is averaged over all twelve experiments used for discovery, and the same experiments support the displayed fitness, term agreement, and posterior predictions. Equation 15 writes a right-hand-side c convention, whereas Tables S3-S4 label uppercase C values and the exact repository README defines those C values in a zero-form equation; if they denote the same fit then c=-C, but neither source states the mapping. Table signs therefore cannot safely be reported as Equation 15 right-hand-side signs. The plots support in-sample descriptive adequacy, not unique identification or out-of-experiment predictive validity.

method.core_idea: Learn a compact probability distribution over physically familiar PDE term combinations from a handbook, then repeatedly bias that distribution toward structures whose fitted derivatives explain the observed field.
method.mechanism: Manually tokenize known equations into alternating terms and operators, augment commutative orderings, and train an autoregressive transformer. Fit a neural surrogate to observations, evaluate generated structures with least-squares coefficients and a sparsity-weighted R-squared reward, fine-tune on elite candidates for five rounds, and optionally refine the winning coefficients with a PINN loss.
assumptions: The unknown law is expressible using the available operator and term vocabulary or a manually extended version of it.
A neural surrogate reconstructs the field and its required derivatives without introducing structure-changing bias.
A high sparsity-weighted R-squared distinguishes the governing equation from correlated or observationally equivalent alternatives.
Handbook co-occurrence patterns transfer from canonical equations to the target physical domain.
Alternating term and operator tokens are expressive enough for the relevant free-form structures.
Five elite fine-tuning cycles explore enough of the stochastic structure space for a reliable optimum.
Available observations cover enough state-space variation to identify coefficients and terms uniquely.

techniques.role: Concentrates candidate generation on term combinations observed across 221 curated PDE structures.
Produces 32 order variants per equation so an autoregressive model is less tied to an arbitrary additive or multiplicative ordering.
Alternates operators and terms, masks unavailable dimensions, and mixes model sampling with uniform exploration.
Uses a smooth neural interpolant and automatic differentiation to turn sparse or noisy observations into regression features.
Retrains the generator on the ten highest-reward structures so later samples concentrate near empirically promising forms.
Combines least-squares R-squared with a logarithmic term-count penalty when ranking candidate structures.
Optimizes coefficients after structure selection through a joint data and PDE residual loss.

evaluations.setting: Eight one-dimensional canonical and handbook PDEs using 10,000 surrogate metadata points.
evaluations.metric: Correct structure, coefficient error, failure threshold under Gaussian noise, and smallest successful observation count.
evaluations.result: All displayed zero-noise structures are recovered; reported noise and data thresholds vary substantially by equation, from no tested noise tolerance for the fractional case to 100% for the wave and Klein-Gordon cases.
evaluations.baseline: Ground-truth equations, with the target structure removed from EqGPT pretraining.

evaluations.setting: Shared-surrogate comparison over eight canonical structures.
evaluations.metric: Structural recovery category and wall-clock time.
evaluations.result: EqGPT is shown correct on all eight in 11.47-37.83 seconds.
evaluations.baseline: PDE-FIND, GGA, DISCOVER, PDE-READ, W-SINDy, LLM4ED, and WeakIdent; most are faster on their supported forms but several complex cases are marked not applicable or incorrect.

evaluations.setting: Poisson equations on disk, smiley-face, discontinuous glyph, and 3D shuttle regions.
evaluations.metric: Recovered structure, reward trajectory, and coefficient error.
evaluations.result: The correct Laplacian or Poisson form is reported in all four demonstrations; the shuttle coefficient error is 0.63% and the EITech case is below 2%.
evaluations.baseline: Known simulated governing equations; no competing method or repeated-seed distribution is shown.

evaluations.setting: 2D Burgers, H-shaped membrane vibration, and 3D coupled oil-water displacement.
evaluations.result: EqGPT returns the target term sets or their expanded forms, though the H-membrane coefficients include a 1.30 multiplier on one spatial derivative and the oil-water coefficients deviate from the simulator equations.
evaluations.baseline: Known simulated equations, without statistical replication.

evaluations.setting: Twelve wave-tank experiments for focused surface waves approaching breaking.
evaluations.metric: Mean discovery reward, per-case regression fitness, term agreement, posterior field prediction, and coefficient variation.
evaluations.result: One three-term nonlinear dispersive equation fits all twelve displayed cases, with per-case coefficients varying and the nonlinear term changing sign in case 12.
evaluations.baseline: Observed fields from the same twelve experiments used to score candidates; no held-out experiment or alternative-law comparison is reported.

evaluations.setting: Target-removal and handbook-size ablations over ten seeds.
evaluations.metric: Exact-structure success rate and first successful optimization epoch.
evaluations.result: Removing a target equation leaves success at or above 0.7 for all eight canonical cases; increasing handbook training structures from 0 toward 220 generally raises success on three tested equations to 0.8-1.0.
evaluations.baseline: EqGPT trained with the target present and EqGPT trained on smaller random handbook subsets.

limitations: Author-stated: performance depends on the quality and coverage of the manually constructed handbook dataset, which can transmit domain bias and omit useful equation families.
Reviewer-identified: the grammar enforces alternating token types and available dimensions but not units, symmetries, conservation, causality, boundary compatibility, or mathematical well-posedness.

Reviewer-identified: neural interpolation and automatic differentiation can make sparse observations appear dense without adding information; derivative bias is not propagated into structural uncertainty.

Reviewer-identified: sparsity-weighted R-squared cannot resolve observationally equivalent PDEs or correlated derivative features, and no uniqueness, stability-selection, or posterior uncertainty analysis is supplied.

Reviewer-identified: the baseline heatmap operates on a shared trained surrogate and marks unsupported expressions as not applicable, so it does not establish end-to-end superiority under matched raw data, tuning effort, compute, or search space.
Reviewer-identified: most irregular, high-dimensional, and multivariable demonstrations show one optimization run without confidence intervals or seed-level success rates.
Reviewer-identified: all twelve wave experiments participate in candidate scoring and evaluation, leaving no held-out physical campaign for the headline new-law claim.

Reviewer-identified: Equation 15, Tables S3-S4, and the repository README use unresolved right-hand-side versus zero-form coefficient conventions, so the tabulated signs cannot be assigned to Equation 15 without an explicit mapping.

Reviewer-identified: the wave analysis compares fit to observations but not identifiability against alternative dispersive or nonlinear equations, predictive stability beyond the measured interval, or conservation behavior.
Reviewer-identified: Equation 17 abbreviates the claimed 43-term baseline library with ellipses, so the paper alone does not exhaustively define that comparison's candidate set.

Reviewer-identified: the pinned arXiv revision predates a materially expanded Nature Communications version of record, so its baseline and robustness evidence should not be silently conflated with the later article.

Reviewer-identified: the current public GitHub head does not compile because surrogate_model.py contains an incomplete assignment; train_gpt.py raises before its direct path and, if that raise is removed, calls train without the required Equation_name argument. The README entry route is therefore not directly runnable, and the release has no automated tests or locked environment file.

Reviewer-identified: the public repository provides canonical and several simulated datasets but omits the wave-tank and oil-water data behind the strongest real-world and multivariable claims; other large simulations are delegated to an external Figshare deposit.
failure_modes: The governing term is absent from the fixed or manually extended vocabulary, so no amount of fine-tuning can generate it.
The surrogate smooths away shocks, discontinuities, or high-frequency content and produces biased high-order derivatives.
Strongly correlated candidate terms yield a high-reward but noncausal or nonunique equation.
Elite fine-tuning collapses generation around an early spurious structure and five rounds are insufficient to escape it.
A dimension-valid token sequence is dimensionally or physically inconsistent despite passing the grammar masks.
Division tokens create singular features, forcing data-row deletion or unstable least-squares coefficients.
Noise perturbs small coefficients enough to add redundant terms or change the recovered structure, as in the 2D Burgers 20% case.
A discovered empirical wave law fits the measured approach-to-breaking interval but becomes unstable or inaccurate outside it.
Manual equation normalization treats physically distinct coefficient regimes or equivalent structures inconsistently, biasing the learned prior.
reusable_insights: A small scientific corpus can be useful as a proposal distribution even when it is far too small for direct supervised data-to-equation learning.
Separate structure proposal from coefficient estimation: symbolic search can operate over discrete forms while regression handles continuous coefficients.
Commutative augmentation is important whenever an autoregressive serialization imposes arbitrary order on an order-invariant object.
Evaluate scientific discovery systems at three layers: reconstruction of the field, identification of the equation, and out-of-sample validation of the inferred law.
Shared preprocessing isolates structure-search cost but must not be presented as evidence for an end-to-end denoising advantage.
A grammar prior should be extended with units, symmetry, conservation, and boundary constraints before calling its outputs physically valid.
Novel-law claims need alternative-model comparison and held-out interventions or experiments, not only posterior replay on discovery data.
Artifact audits should check compilation, entry points, complete headline datasets, fixed seeds, and environment locks in addition to the paper's code-availability statement.
open_questions: How much of EqGPT's gain comes from handbook co-occurrence learning versus the hard vocabulary, grammar masks, and elite search loop?
Can uncertainty in the surrogate and its derivatives be propagated into a posterior over PDE structures and coefficients?
Would a units-aware or symmetry-equivariant grammar reduce false candidates without excluding genuinely new laws?
How does the method compare under matched raw observations, search budget, hardware, and hyperparameter tuning across baselines that support the same expression class?
Does the wave equation predict a completely held-out campaign, later breaking stages, or changed depth and spectral regimes better than established alternatives?
Which alternative equations are observationally indistinguishable from the selected wave law over the three disconnected camera regions?
Can the handbook extraction and equivalence normalization be automated and independently audited without changing the learned prior?
How does success scale with vocabulary size, equation length, number of state variables, and derivative order beyond the selected demonstrations?
Can an executable artifact reproduce every main and supplementary figure from clean checkout with fixed seeds and recorded hardware?

competitive_landscape.title: Any equation is a forest: Symbolic genetic algorithm for discovering open-form partial differential equations (SGA-PDE)
competitive_landscape.difference: SGA-PDE evolves binary-tree terms and forest equations with a genetic algorithm and no learned handbook prior; EqGPT serializes terms into a compact grammar and uses pretrained sampling plus elite fine-tuning, trading tree expressiveness for a narrower, faster proposal space.

competitive_landscape.title: DISCOVER: Deep identification of symbolically concise open-form PDEs via enhanced reinforcement-learning
competitive_landscape.difference: DISCOVER trains a structure-aware recurrent agent with reinforcement learning over symbolic expression trees; EqGPT pretrains an autoregressive sequence model on handbook structures and updates it with the top ten candidates, avoiding policy-gradient tree search but imposing a more handcrafted vocabulary grammar.

competitive_landscape.title: PDE-READ: Human-readable Partial Differential Equation Discovery using Deep Learning
competitive_landscape.difference: PDE-READ jointly learns a solution network and hidden PDE network, then extracts a polynomial-library equation with recursive feature elimination; EqGPT searches free-form token combinations after fitting a surrogate and can vary the left-hand term, but lacks PDE-READ's explicit discussion of non-identifiability.

competitive_landscape.title: WeakIdent: Weak formulation for Identifying Differential Equations using Narrow-fit and Trimming
competitive_landscape.difference: WeakIdent transfers derivatives to test functions and trims a predefined feature library to gain noise robustness without neural interpolation; EqGPT broadens the structure space through generative tokens but depends on pointwise high-order derivatives of a learned surrogate.

competitive_landscape.title: PDE-GANet: Partial differential equation discovery powered by adversarial learning
competitive_landscape.difference: PDE-GANet couples symbolic-network generators to recurrent discriminators and bidirectional solution-consistency losses, jointly evaluating expressions through generated trajectories; EqGPT ranks discrete handbook-guided structures by surrogate-feature regression and does not jointly learn a forward solver during search.
competitive_landscape.source_version: Neural Networks 196 (2026), article 108387, version of record

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The paper claims a knowledge-guided generative PDE-discovery framework that learns broad structural regularities from a mathematical handbook, efficiently generates free-form differential terms, and uses them to reveal a previously unreported wave-breaking law.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The exact cached revision demonstrates a new composition of handbook-derived sequence pretraining, constrained PDE token generation, regression rewards, and elite fine-tuning across canonical, irregular-domain, high-dimensional, multivariable, and wave-tank examples.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The defensible novelty is the use of a curated PDE handbook as a learned proposal prior inside an iterative structure-search loop. Autoregressive symbolic generation, surrogate differentiation, sparse rewards, genetic or reinforcement search, and PINN coefficient refinement all predate the work. The wave equation is an interesting empirical hypothesis, but absent held-out experiments, alternative-law comparison, and a complete executable artifact, it should not yet be treated as a uniquely established new governing law.

reviewer_notes: Every page, displayed equation, table, figure, and supplementary panel in the pinned 38-page arXiv v1 artifact was inspected, and an independent second pass reproduced its exact PDF and text hashes. Equation 1 defines reward=(1-alpha0 log10 Nterm)R^2. Equation 15 prints eta_t*=c1 eta_x*+c2 eta_xxx*+c3(eta*^2)_xxx, but the table and repository zero-form sign conventions are not reconciled. Current-source checks found a Nature Communications version of record published 2025-11-21 (DOI 10.1038/s41467-025-65114-2) that materially expands the baseline and robustness discussion and adds a Zenodo deposit; those later results were used only to contextualize version drift, not as evidence attributed to this pinned v1 reading. The current GitHub repository was inspected at commit dc35fc0ac860ff224293f01d2a62204042095127 (2026-04-23): it contains the 221-equation workbook, core scripts, several canonical and irregular-domain datasets, and one KdV output example, but no automated tests or environment lock; Python compilation fails at code/surrogate_model.py:307, and code/train_gpt.py both raises before its direct path and later omits a required train argument. The repository does not contain the wave-tank or oil-water datasets; shuttle and H-membrane data are delegated to Figshare DOI 10.6084/m9.figshare.27195066. Primary records for SGA-PDE, DISCOVER, PDE-READ, WeakIdent, and the subsequent PDE-GANet were checked on 2026-08-24.

The pass reproduced headline results while correcting the H-membrane formula, shuttle interval, oil-water operator notation, wave coefficient convention, abbreviated baseline library, and two broken execution paths.
